block.alchemia.infusion_matrix.lopsided: Awake, but the ring pulls one way (%s)
block.alchemia.infusion_matrix.nothing: What is laid out here makes nothing
block.alchemia.levitator.range: Range set to %s blocks (%s aer a minute for each thing lifted)
block.alchemia.mirror.already_linked: That mirror is already linked to a valid destination.
entity.alchemia.golem.not_yours: This does not belong to you
flux_event.alchemia.sickness: The local aura momentarily becomes unstable, hampering your magical ability.
flux_event.alchemia.warp: The nearby aura suddenly twists and warps, leaving your thoughts in a shambles.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.alchemists_fire.n: Whatever it sets alight burns far longer.
Whatever it touches is chilled as well as hurt, and walks away slowly.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.architect.note: The square the focus will work on is shown and can be set, rather than guessed at.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.bat_bombs.note: The bats always burst, and burst harder.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.chain_lightning.n: Slower and harder, and the bolt jumps on to whatever is standing near what it struck.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.devil_bats.note: Bigger bats that never burst and keep at their mark until one of them is done.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.dowsing.note: Ore sometimes comes up as a cluster, which smelts to twice as much.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.earth_shock.note: A ball lobbed at the ground instead of a bolt, which leaves the ground live for a while.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.enlarge.note: Wider, or more of them at once, depending on what the focus does to begin with.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.extend.note: Whatever the focus leaves behind on what it touches stays longer.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.fireball.note: A ball to throw instead of a spray to hold down. It costs eight times as much and waits a second.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.firebeam.note: The spray drawn into a line. Narrower, hotter, and it burns through what stands in it.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.frugal.note: A tenth off the bill per rank. It pays for this focus's own working and nothing else.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.ice_boulder.note: One boulder, which bounces. Where it ends up is partly the thrower's skill.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.nightshade.note: All three curses at once rather than whichever one the burst happens to pick.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.persistent.note: When its mark is gone the splinter finds another of the same kind rather than falling.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.potency.note: Harder. About a fifth more per rank, though each focus counts that its own way.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.scattershot.note: A volley of splinters instead of one spike. Each is little; together they are not.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.seeker.note: The orb goes straight at the nearest living thing instead of wandering, and never goes wrong.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.silk_touch.note: The block comes up as it stood rather than as what it breaks into. It is not cheap.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.sticky.note: The hook does not let go on arrival. Letting go is the climber's business.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.treasure.note: More out of what is broken, the way fortune and looting give more.
focus_upgrade.alchemia.vampire_bats.note: The bats drink what they bite, and hand some of it back to whoever called them.
golem.alchemia.addon.armored.text: Plates of its own material all over it, as heavy as they are.
golem.alchemia.addon.fighter.text: An aggression module, so that it will fight.
golem.alchemia.addon.hauler.text: A frame on its back for a second stack of things.
golem.alchemia.arm.basic.text: Plain arms and hands, with nothing for or against them.
golem.alchemia.arm.breakers.text: Arms ending in a pair of diamond-tipped grinders driven by pistons.
golem.alchemia.arm.claws.text: Arms ending in a pair of sharp metal pincers, with an aggression module built in.
golem.alchemia.arm.darts.text: Arms ending in launchers that make their own darts, with an aggression module built in.
golem.alchemia.arm.fine.text: Arms ending in small, careful hands.
golem.alchemia.head.basic.text: The plain head, with nothing for or against it.
golem.alchemia.head.scout.text: The clockwork head with a vision module for eyes.
golem.alchemia.head.smart.text: A bioalchemic mind in a head: it thinks and learns, but breaks easily.
golem.alchemia.head.smart_armored.text: The smart head, plated and padded so that it is no longer fragile.
golem.alchemia.head.smart_scout.text: A bioalchemic mind behind a vision module's eyes: the best a golem's head can be.
golem.alchemia.leg.climber.text: Legs fitted with flint grips, for going up walls.
golem.alchemia.leg.flyer.text: An arcane levitator to float the golem about, a third more slowly.
golem.alchemia.leg.roller.text: One wheel: quick, but it cannot step up as high.
golem.alchemia.leg.walker.text: Plain legs, with nothing for or against them.
golem.alchemia.material.alchemium.text: Everything iron is and more: it takes more and is better armoured, and is just as heavy.
golem.alchemia.material.brass.text: Not so sturdy as iron, and it burns, but brass lets a frame be built light.
golem.alchemia.material.clay.text: Baked clay: not strong, but it does not burn, and it is not heavy.
golem.alchemia.material.iron.text: Sturdy, fireproof and hard to blow apart, but heavy.
golem.alchemia.material.void.text: A little softer than iron and nowhere near as heavy, and it mends itself.
golem.alchemia.material.wood.text: Light and quick, but there is not much to it.
golem.alchemia.prop.empty: Click where the block has gone
golem.alchemia.prop.lock: Only golems of the seal's owner work it
golem.alchemia.trait.armored.text: Half as much armour again, or one more at least. Armored and fragile cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.blastproof.text: Takes a third of what an explosion would do to it, and never more than half its health at once.
golem.alchemia.trait.brutal.text: Hits half as hard again, or one harder at least.
golem.alchemia.trait.climber.text: Goes straight up a wall when it has to, and is never hurt by a fall.
golem.alchemia.trait.clumsy.text: Hands good for little more than the plainest handling. Clumsy and deft cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.deft.text: Fine fingers, for work that wants a light touch. Deft and clumsy cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.fighter.text: It will turn on things and strike them.
golem.alchemia.trait.fireproof.text: Fire and lava do nothing to it.
golem.alchemia.trait.flyer.text: Floats wherever it goes, and is never hurt by a fall, but goes more slowly than it would walk.
golem.alchemia.trait.fragile.text: A quarter less health and armour. Fragile and armored cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.hauler.text: Carries two stacks of things rather than one.
golem.alchemia.trait.heavy.text: Slower for its weight. Heavy and light cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.light.text: Quicker for being light. Light and heavy cancel each other.
golem.alchemia.trait.repair.text: Mends itself more than twice as fast as other golems.
golem.alchemia.trait.scout.text: Sees further, and goes twice as far from home about its work: thirty-two blocks rather than sixteen.
golem.alchemia.trait.smart.text: Thinks for itself more than a golem ought to, and learns from what it does, coming on a rank at a time.
golem.alchemia.trait.wheeled.text: Rolls rather than walks: quicker, but it cannot step up as high.
gui.alchemia.no_wand: A wand must be laid on the bench
gui.alchemia.not_enough_vis: The wand does not hold enough
gui.alchemia.not_researched: You do not know how this is made
item.alchemia.autocaster.note: Fires a fitted focus on its own
item.alchemia.elemental_shovel.laying.1: Laying upright out of the face
item.alchemia.elemental_shovel.laying.2: Laying across out of the face

pack.alchemia.legacy.title: Original Thaumcraft Assets
research.alchemia.alchemium_gear.page: The metal is worth forging with. A tool of it cuts about as fast as diamond, lasts twice what iron does, and takes an enchantment better than anything that can be dug up. A suit of it stops what iron stops and outlasts diamond by half again. Nothing about the shapes is new -- the sticks go where they always went.
research.alchemia.alchemium_smelter.page: A smelter plated in alchemium. It boils things down no faster, but it loses less of what comes off them, and it pours what it holds up into the alembics above more quickly.
research.alchemia.alumentum.page: Coal that has been round again. What comes out of the water holds four times the fire it went in with, and in an essentia smelter it does one thing more: the work goes a fifth quicker while it lasts. A slow furnace is the price of a smelter, and this is the one thing that can be spent against it.
research.alchemia.amber.page: Sap that hardened around something long ago, and held it there. It breaks out of the ore whole, and takes a polish that the stone around it never will.
research.alchemia.arcane_bore.page: A machine that carries an excavation focus further than any wand, and without anyone standing over it. It goes directly above or below its base; point it with a wand and give it a redstone signal, and it eats a tunnel out the way it faces, sixty-four blocks deep, sweeping a spiral as it goes. It wants an excavation focus in its left slot and any pickaxe in its right: whatever is worked into either -- force, efficiency, widening, treasure, fortune, silk touch, dowsing -- goes into what it mines. The pickaxe wears a point a block, and the bore stops while it has one left. Everything mined comes out of the base's nozzle, into a container there if there is one; a wand on the base turns the nozzle. Entropy piped into the base drives it fast, twenty blocks a point; without it, it draws entropy out of the air, a block a point and far slower.
research.alchemia.arcane_ear.page: An ear that hears note blocks. Tune it as you would a note block, a click a semitone up; it listens in the voice of whatever it is fixed to, the way a note block plays in the voice of what it stands on. When a note block within sixty-four blocks plays its note, it gives a short, full redstone pulse, through what it is fixed to as well. It can be fixed to any face.
research.alchemia.arcane_lamp.page: A lamp of brass and amber that lights more than itself. Every quarter of a second it sets a point of light down somewhere dark within fifteen blocks, where it can see, so that over a few minutes the cave or cellar round it fills with light from nowhere in particular. Hang it from any face. A redstone signal puts it out, and every light it set down goes out with it.
research.alchemia.arcane_stone.page: Common stone with a shard worked into it, and it stops being common. It takes the aura the way a wick takes oil, which is why every worthwhile structure in this craft is built of it.
research.alchemia.arcane_workbench.page: A bench with a cloth laid over it and a place to set a wand down. What is shaped here costs vis as well as materials, and the vis comes out of the wand — so the bench is only ever as good as what is lying on it.
research.alchemia.aspects.page: Everything is made of six primal essences and the things they combine into. An alchemometer will name them for you, one object at a time, and what it names is written down here as you go.
research.alchemia.aura_totem.page: It is high time the things you have learned about the aura were put to use. The Totem of Dispersal takes vis from round itself and spreads it over a wider area. Feed it vis shards: each burns for a while, and says what kind of vis it moves -- a balanced shard moves all six primals. Meddling with the aura is not without risk, and now and then what it moves turns to flux instead. A totem works on an inner area, alone its own chunk, and an outer one, alone the eight chunks round that; the totem of dispersal moves vis from the inner out to the outer. Up to five totem poles can stand under it. Each inner pole widens the inner area by a chunk all round, each outer pole the outer, and either makes it work a little faster -- and a little likelier to make flux. A dispersal totem with one inner and two outer poles draws from the three chunks by three about it and spreads into a ring three chunks wide beyond that.
research.alchemia.aura_totem_pole_pure.p: A totem pole that steadies the totem it holds up, making it less likely to spoil what it moves into flux. It neither widens nor quickens anything.
research.alchemia.aura_totem_pull.page: The Totem of Attraction works much as the Totem of Dispersal does, but the other way: it draws vis in from the outer area and moves it into the inner.
research.alchemia.autocaster.page: A focus on a bracket, with enough of a mind in it to pick something and point itself at it. It is not a thaumaturge: it draws its own vis out of the air a drop at a time, holds a hundred of each primal at most, and nothing worn or carried makes a working any cheaper for it. Seven of the twelve foci are worth aiming at a thing, and those are the seven it will take. It goes against any face -- floor, wall or ceiling -- and it is told what to mind: animals, monsters, people, and whatever is already yours. A wand clicked against it takes it back down, focus and all.
research.alchemia.bath_salts.page: Warp is a danger to the most careful of thaumaturges, and for those who have dabbled a little too much its effects are more than a nuisance. These salts help. Toss them into still water and when they dissolve the water turns to a silvery purifying fluid. Step into it and it soothes away the day, warding you against warp for a while; it is used up doing so. The deeper warp has set in, the shorter the ward. The salts are fragile, and dissolve within ten seconds of being dropped, wherever they lie.
research.alchemia.bellows.page: Two boards and a hide, with a nozzle. Set against a furnace they hurry what is in it by half again. Set against an essentia smelter from the side or the back they cut the time it takes to boil anything down by an eighth apiece, three at most. They pump for as long as nothing stops them, and a redstone signal does. They blow the way you were looking when you put them down; crouch to turn them round.
research.alchemia.bioalchemic_mind.page: The clockwork mind with something living grown into it on the altar. What comes out can be told to choose rather than only to follow, and the things that have to decide for themselves -- an autocaster picking its mark -- are built round one.
research.alchemia.brain_jar.page: A zombie's brain, woken and sealed in a warded jar. It keeps some of its hunger, and though it cannot eat brains any more it enjoys the thoughts and experience of whatever dies nearby, drawing them in from six blocks off, up to two thousand. A good shake makes it give some back. When it is full it lets off wisps. It counts as two bookshelves to an enchanting table.
research.alchemia.centrifuge.page: Compound essentia piped in from below is spun until it comes apart, and one of the two things it was made of, either one, is drawn off the top. Only one: the other half is lost in the spinning. It holds one point coming in and one going out, takes nothing while either is full, and will not take the six primals, which have nothing to come apart into. It never pushes; something above has to draw on it. A redstone signal stops it.
research.alchemia.charger.page: Four posts and a crystal, standing over a workbench. It fills the wand left below it and does nothing else — no faster than a hand would, but a hand has other work to do.
research.alchemia.clockwork_mind.page: Gears and a comparator under glass, plated in brass. It is not a mind in any way that matters, but it will follow one rule without being told twice, which is all a machine needs -- a golem most of all. Golems are made at a golem press. Stand a piston facing up with iron bars on it, a stone table beside it, an anvil beside the table and a cauldron beside the anvil and the piston, the four making a square, and strike any of it with a wand. Pick at the press what the golem is to be made of and the parts it is to have: it takes what they need from your pack, and presses it a measure of machina at a time, drawn up a tube or straight out of a jar set against it.
research.alchemia.control_seals.page: Golems are given work with seals: clay and tallow worked with a red dye and a nitor, then steeped in a crucible into a seal that does one thing. Stuck to the face of a block, a seal offers tasks to any golem nearby that can do them, the nearest and most urgent first. Hold a seal, a golem or a golemancer's bell to see the seals about you, and crouch to see them through walls. Ring the bell at a seal to set it up: how urgent it is, whether only golems of one colour work it, whether only your own golems may, whether redstone stops it, and whatever else that kind of seal has. Ring it crouching to take the seal down.
research.alchemia.crucible.page: A pot of water kept over a fire. Anything dropped into it comes apart into what it is made of, and once the right things are floating in the water, one last thing thrown in boils the lot into something new.
research.alchemia.crystallizer.page: Essentia piped in at its back is set into crystals one point at a time, which come out of the other end into whatever container stands there, or onto the ground. Any aspect will do. It works on earth drawn out of the air, four points at a time; with none in the air it simply waits. A redstone signal stops it.
research.alchemia.dioptra.page: A device that shows the aura round it plainly. Set a vis shard in the crystal on its top and it draws, in the air over itself, a map thirteen chunks across of how strong that aspect is in each; a balanced shard shows whichever primal is strongest in each chunk instead. Chunks with a node in them sparkle now and then -- not precise, but a help in finding them. A comparator reads how strong the aura is in its own chunk, and a redstone signal puts it out.
research.alchemia.distillation.page: Burning a thing is a crude way to ask what it is made of, but it is an honest one. A smelter sends the answer up as smoke, and alembics stacked above it catch that smoke one aspect at a time.
research.alchemia.elemental_tools.page: Alchemium tools with a primal bound into each on the altar, and what that element is in a tool already worked into them. The axe of the stream fells a tree from its top and sends what falls to whoever felled it, and held up it draws every loose thing nearby in. The pickaxe of the core refines ore into clusters now and then, sounds out the stone it is tapped against, and sets alight whatever it strikes. The sword of the zephyr carries a blow on to what is standing about, and held up it raises a whirlwind that lifts its bearer and throws back anything that comes close. The shovel of the earthmover digs three by three, and used against a face it lays three by three of that same block out of the bag; the setting key turns which way the square stands. The hoe of growth tills three by three and makes things grow where there is nothing to till. Crouch with any of them and it is only a tool.
research.alchemia.enchanted_fabric.page: Wool and string are worked together at the bench with a little of all six primals, and what comes off is cloth that will hold a working the way a wand holds vis. Nothing is made of it that could not be made of cloth; what is different is that it does not forget.
research.alchemia.fertility_lamp.page: An arcane lamp worked on with gold, wheat and carrots. It burns victus, piped in through the face it hangs from, and every fifteen seconds it sets two grown animals of the same kind within seven blocks to courting, at two points a pair. It leaves a pen of more than seven of a kind alone.
research.alchemia.focal_manipulator.page: A bench for working one more thing into a focus. Five things will go into any focus, one to a rank, and which are on offer depends on the focus and on how deep the rank is -- the shallow ones give a focus more of what it already does, and the deep ones turn it into something else. The price is levels paid up front and vis drawn out of the air afterwards, a little every few ticks, so the bench wants a thick sky above it and a while to work. Take the focus off the bench part-way and the work is lost.
research.alchemia.fortress_armour.page: A finished suit of alchemium goes under the matrix and comes back out as plate. It stops what void metal stops and lasts as long as the alchemium it was, which no single metal manages, and no enchanting table will ever be offered better steel. The more of the four is worn the less any one blow gets through, and a blow of fire or a blast is turned worse than a blade is. Falling does not wear it at all -- whatever the ground does to the wearer, it does nothing to the plate.
research.alchemia.goggles.page: Two alchemometers looking through brass. An aura node is invisible to anyone not wearing a pair, which makes these the first thing to build and the last thing to take off: half of what this craft is built on cannot be seen at all until they are on your face.
research.alchemia.golem_alchemium.page: Everything iron is and more of it: an alchemium golem takes more, is better armoured and hits harder, and is just as heavy.
research.alchemia.golem_brass.page: Brass is not as sturdy as iron and it burns, but it lets a frame be built light, and a brass golem is quick. Knowing brass is also how fine manipulators are made.
research.alchemia.golem_breaker.page: Arms ending in diamond-tipped grinders, driven by pistons. A golem with them is clumsy and hits hard, and can break most blocks.
research.alchemia.golem_clay.page: Terracotta is not strong, but a golem baked of it does not burn, and is no heavier for that.
research.alchemia.golem_climber.page: Legs fitted with flint grips go straight up whatever is in the way, and a golem on them is never hurt by a fall.
research.alchemia.golem_combat.page: With the aggression module worked out, golems can be built for fighting: claw arms that snap shut and hit hard, dart launchers that make their own darts and shoot from up to sixteen blocks, armour plating of the golem's own material, an armoured smart head that is no longer fragile, and an aggression module fitted to any golem at all.
research.alchemia.golem_direct.page: A golem left to itself keeps within sixteen blocks of where it was set down. Ring a golemancer's bell at one of your own and it follows you instead; ring it again and it stays where it is, and that is its home from then on. A golem answers only to its owner. A wand put to it folds it back into an item, with all it has learned, and a dye colours the little flag on its back.
research.alchemia.golem_flyer.page: An arcane levitator under a golem floats it wherever it goes. It is a third slower for it, and fragile, but nothing on the ground is in its way and it never comes to harm by falling.
research.alchemia.golem_iron.page: Iron plate makes a golem sturdy, fireproof and hard to blow apart, at the cost of being heavy and slow. Three iron ingots in a row make three plates.
research.alchemia.golem_vision.page: Glass bottles and fermented spider eyes set in brass make a vision module, a pair of eyes for a golem's head. A golem that sees further works further from home, thirty-two blocks rather than sixteen, though a head with such eyes in it is fragile.
research.alchemia.golem_void.page: Void metal is a little softer than iron and nowhere near as heavy, and a golem made of it mends itself more than twice as fast as any other. Its gears are made as the others are, of nuggets round an iron ingot.
research.alchemia.golem_wood.page: A golem is a made thing, pressed whole out of a frame and the parts fitted to it, and it belongs to whoever sets it down. Everyone starts with greatwood: light and quick, and not much to it. What a golem is made of decides how much it can take, how hard it hits, and something of what it is like.
research.alchemia.greatwood.page: A tree that grows broader and older than any other. Its trunk thickens where lesser wood would split, and a single one will keep a workshop in timber for a season.
research.alchemia.growth_lamp.page: An arcane lamp worked on with gold and bone meal. It burns herba, piped in through the face it hangs from, and every point is a hundred nudges to whatever is still growing within six blocks -- each nudge one more turn of growing, taken or not as the plant would take it anyway. It goes dark when it runs out.
research.alchemia.hungry_chest.page: A chest in every way, except that whatever comes to rest on its lid it eats: whole stacks where there is room, part of one where there is only room for part. What will not fit stays where it fell. It never pairs into a double chest.
Two things to set against a smelter's sides or back. An auxiliary slurry pump draws on what the smelter holds and pours it up into alembics stacked on the pump itself, so one fire fills another column for every pump. An auxiliary venting port catches some of what the smelter loses before it gets into the air: a third with one, more with each one after, though less each time.
research.alchemia.infernal_furnace.page: A furnace of obsidian and nether brick round a heart of lava, which needs no fuel. Build it three blocks every way: nether brick at the corners, obsidian on the edges and the floor, still lava in the middle with air above it, and iron bars in place of one of the four obsidian blocks beside the lava. Work it with a wand. Things dropped in through the top are smelted and spat out where the bars were; anything that will not smelt is burned to nothing. It is slow on its own, and much quicker on fire drawn out of the air; bellows blowing into it from two blocks out make it quicker still. Ores come out with a nugget besides now and then, more often with bellows. A little flux escapes now and again.
research.alchemia.infusion_boost.page: Two stones, laid a course below the altar's corners, and an altar takes whatever is under them without being asked. One hurries a turn along and charges a little more for it; the other waits longer and charges less. Four of a kind is the whole of either -- twelve ticks to a turn, or eight parts in a hundred off the bill -- and nothing takes a working below half price. They can be mixed, which is the only reason there are two of them rather than one with a switch.
research.alchemia.infusion_enchantment.p: An altar will put on a tool what no table will sell. There is no gambling and no book to keep it in: the tool goes under the matrix, the price is paid in essentia, and it comes back with one more thing about it. Collector sends what is broken to the one who broke it. Destructive takes the eight blocks round the one struck, where the tool would have served for them anyway. Burrowing brings a seam or a trunk apart from its far end. Refining makes ore come up now and then as a cluster, which smelts to twice the metal. Sounding taps the stone and shows what is behind it for a moment, at five swings' wear. Arcing carries a blow to whatever is standing beside what was struck. Essence makes what is killed give up a little of what it was made of -- the one way to essentia that wants no smelter, and so the meanest of them. Crouch and the digging ones go quiet.
research.alchemia.jar_label.page: Essentia will not sit in the open. A warded jar holds sixty-four of one kind and refuses the rest; a label tells it which kind before there is any, so a shelf can be laid out empty and filled later. A brace lets a jar be filled and never emptied.
research.alchemia.levitator.page: Not flight, but the next best thing. A levitator lifts whatever is in front of it -- things dropped, animals, you -- up to eight blocks, or as far as the first solid block. Crouch over one and you are let down slowly. Put on its side it pushes along instead, holding up what it pushes; put it down facing whichever way you like, crouching to turn it round. It burns aer from the aura while it is carrying anything, more the further it reaches: an empty hand on it steps its range through four, eight, sixteen and thirty-two blocks. A redstone signal stops it.
research.alchemia.metallurgy.page: Iron does not want to be anything else, and a crucible is how you argue with it. Steeped in earth and order it comes out alchemium; in energy and water, brass.
research.alchemia.mirror.page: Two mirrors made a pair pass to each other whatever is thrown or piped into either -- even from one world to another -- but never anything living. Put one up, hold a second against it, then put the second up wherever it should open. A pair is two and only two. A mirror taken down remembers its partner, and either can be put up again elsewhere. Moving things strains the aura, and the more is moved the more flux it lets out.
research.alchemia.mirror_essentia.page: Essentia cannot be piped through a mirror. But an essentia mirror stands in for whatever essentia is held within eight blocks in front of its partner, so that an altar or a lamp reaching for essentia near one draws on jars by the other. It strains the aura as the other mirrors do.
research.alchemia.mirror_hand.page: A mirror on a handle. Held against a magic mirror it remembers it, even one already paired; opened anywhere, whatever is put in it comes out of that mirror. It only sends, never receives.
research.alchemia.nitor.page: Light with nothing burning under it. It never goes out and never wants feeding, which is worth the glowstone it costs, and it hangs wherever it is put -- floor, wall, ceiling, open air. A flame that needed something to stand on would be a torch. A dye put to one changes its colour and nothing else; there are sixteen and none is the original.
research.alchemia.primal_charm.page: Where artifice starts: a shard of every primal and the balanced shard that holds them, worked round a ring of gold. Nothing much is done with a charm on its own; a great deal is built round one. Quicksilver laid on the back of a pane of glass makes a mirror, which is the other thing nearly every device needs.
research.alchemia.primal_crusher.page: Both elemental diggers and both of their void-metal counterparts beaten together round something that should not be able to hold all four. What comes out is a pickaxe and a shovel at once that digs three by three and refines ore as it goes. It has lost the building and the sounding; what is left only breaks things. Like void metal it mends itself, a point a second, and unlike anything else it is uneasy in the hand -- it carries two points of warp while it is held.
research.alchemia.quicksilver.page: A metal that will not keep still, coaxed out of cinnabar by fire. It pools rather than sits, and every alchemist learns early to keep a lid on it.
research.alchemia.recharge_pedestal.page: Travelling the countryside to fill a wand is all very well, but a pedestal that does it for you is better. Set a wand on it and it draws vis from the aura of its chunk to fill it, as much as a wand held in the hand would, twice a second. Like a wand in the hand, it leaves alone any aura run down below a tenth of what it should be. A hopper can set a wand on it and take one off.
research.alchemia.redstone_relay.page: Redstone is known to dull magic; sent through a vis crystal, it can be made to do only as much of that as you like. The relay is put down and wired like a repeater, its output the end with the torch. It has two toggles. The one at the back sets how strong a signal it needs before it answers; the one beside the torch, how strong a signal it gives out when it does. Each steps from one to fifteen.
research.alchemia.robes.page: A robe stops arrows about as well as a shirt does. That is not what it is for. Cloth that remembers a working sits between a wand and the air it draws from, and every price the wand is asked comes down a little. Two parts in a hundred at the chest and at the legs, one at the feet. There is no hood: a head wants something else on it, and the robe was never cut for one.
research.alchemia.seal_break.page: Golems with grinder arms break every block in the seal's area that its one filter entry lets by. Each block takes half a second of grinding for every three points of its hardness, and drops what it would have to the right tool.
research.alchemia.seal_butcher.page: Every ten seconds, smart fighting golems take one grown animal from any herd of more than two in the seal's area, leaving the young, the tame and the last two alone. A herd is thinned, never ended.
research.alchemia.seal_collect.page: Golems pick up whatever lies still in the area in front of the seal and its filter lets by, as much as they can carry. The area can be widened up to eight blocks each way. The advanced seal, steeped again with mind and senses, has nine filter entries and its own options, and only smart golems work it. Clumsy golems cannot pick anything up.
research.alchemia.seal_empty.page: Stuck on a container, golems take out of it whatever the filter lets by, as much as they can carry, through the face the seal is on. What they then do with it is up to other seals. It can be set to leave one of each thing behind. The advanced seal can work through its whitelist an entry at a time, and only smart golems work it.
research.alchemia.seal_guard.page: An aggression module -- blaze powder behind glass, on brass -- gives a golem the will to fight, and a guarding seal tells it what at. Fighting golems go for whatever monster comes into the seal's area. The advanced seal, for smart golems, can be set on animals too, and on players where the server allows it.
research.alchemia.seal_harvest.page: Deft, smart golems take whatever has ripened in the seal's area: grown crops, melons and pumpkins, the upper parts of sugar cane and cactus, ripe nether wart and cocoa. Berries are picked and left on the bush. Set to replant, the golem plants again whatever it cut, tilling the ground if it has gone back to dirt, and can ask providing seals for the seed.
research.alchemia.seal_lumber.page: Smart golems with grinder arms take down every tree whose logs reach into the seal's area, a log at a time from the crown down, so that nothing is ever left hanging.
research.alchemia.seal_provide.page: Stuck on a container, it answers other seals within sixty-four blocks that need something to work with: when one asks for something this seal's filter lets by and the container has it, a golem that works for the asking seal fetches it out. It can hand out one at a time and leave one behind. Only smart golems work it.
research.alchemia.seal_store.page: Golems carrying something the filter lets by bring it here and put it in, through the face the seal is on; on something that is not a container they drop it in front. With a whitelist, how many of each thing are on the filter is how many are wanted here, and no more are brought; click a filter square with nothing in hand to raise it and right-click to lower it. The advanced seal can be set to bring only what is already there, and only smart golems work it.
research.alchemia.seal_use.page: A deft, smart golem uses what it carries on the block the seal is stuck to, through the face it is on, as a player would with a right click, or a left click if set so. It can use an empty hand, click crouching, work only where the block has gone, and ask providing seals for whatever is on its whitelist. What the click leaves in its hand it keeps.
research.alchemia.silverwood.page: Pale wood that draws the aura to itself, and glows faintly for it. Little that is unnatural will settle near one, which makes a grove of them a quiet place to work.
research.alchemia.spa.page: Throwing salts into water is a chore, easily done away with. The spa takes water, by bucket or by pipe from any side, and bath salts, through its panel or from a hopper on any side but the top, and every two seconds mixes a bucket of the one with a dose of the other and pumps it into the pool above. The pool spreads a block at a time to five by five, wherever there is floor. Switched over on its panel it pumps whatever is in its tank, unmixed -- nearly any liquid that can stand in the world. A redstone signal stops it.
research.alchemia.tallow.page: Rotten flesh stewed in a crucible with a little fire renders down to a clean, waxy tallow, which holds an arcane charge well. It is what control seals are made with.
research.alchemia.thaumatorium.page: A crucible that works on its own. Stand two blocks of brass on a crucible and work them with a wand, from the side you want it to face: what it makes comes out of that side, into a container there if there is one, onto the ground if not. Put a catalyst in it and choose, from the recipes you know that catalyst finishes, what it is to make; it draws the essentia up the pipes itself, an aspect at a time, and as long as there is catalyst it makes the thing perfectly, every time. The crucible under it needs no water, but it does need heat: lava, fire or a nitor directly below. It keeps one recipe in mind; every mnemonic matrix fixed to its sides or top, facing in, lets it keep two more. A redstone signal stops it.
research.alchemia.traveller_boots.page: They stop almost nothing. What they are worth is the walking: a step up a whole block without jumping, a push along the ground, a hold on the air that is not quite flying, and a fall that is forgotten as fast as it happens. Somebody who spends the day between a works and a mine will not take them off for a suit that stops arrows.
research.alchemia.tube_filter.page: Four ways of telling a length of pipe what to do with what passes through it: let one thing by and turn the rest back, let it by one way only, let it by half as fast, or keep a little in hand for when the works wants it.
research.alchemia.tubes.page: Brass pipe with glass in the middle of it. The far end does the pulling rather than the near one, so a run fills whatever still has room instead of whatever it reached first. A valve on the line shuts it, by hand or by redstone.
research.alchemia.vis_crystals.page: Where the aura runs thick, it settles into stone as crystal. Each shade of crystal carries the essence it grew out of, and the stone around it remembers that too.
research.alchemia.void_gear.page: The other sort of good. It cuts faster and hits harder than anything, reaches what netherite reaches, and wears out in a hundred and fifty swings. A suit of it stops nearly what diamond stops and goes to pieces faster than leather. It is not the better metal; it is the metal for the one job that has to be done now.
research.alchemia.void_metal.page: A seed steeped in darkness stops being a seed, and what it becomes, steeped again in metal, sets as an ingot. It will not set at all without a point of flux in the water: the metal wants something wrong in it. What is drawn from it gives back a third of every working, and the caps drawn from it are the last a wand will ever want.
research.alchemia.void_robes.page: A suit of void metal taken apart on the altar and sewn back onto cloth. It stops what the metal stopped and comes apart as fast as the metal did, and in exchange it takes five parts in a hundred off every price, at each of its three pieces. This one has a hood and no boots -- the metal never made a good shoe, and the robe never made a good helm until there was metal to line it with.
research.alchemia.void_smelter.page: A smelter plated in void metal. Almost nothing that comes off what it burns is lost.
research.alchemia.wand.page: A rod with a cap at each end, and nothing else. The caps let vis in and out; the rod decides how much of it will sit still. Held in a hand it fills itself from the air, slowly, wherever the aura has not been worked out.
research.alchemia.wand_cap_alchemium.pag: Metal that has been taught what it is for. A tenth of every working comes back, which is the first time a cap has given anything rather than taken it.
research.alchemia.wand_cap_brass.page: An alloy that pulls harder at the air than either metal in it. It spends no better than gold, but it fills faster, which over a long afternoon is the same thing.
research.alchemia.wand_cap_gold.page: Iron grips vis badly and lets a tenth of every working slip. Gold does not. It is softer and dearer and worth both, for the first cap that does not charge for the privilege.
research.alchemia.wand_rod_greatwood.pag: Cut from a tree that grew slowly and held on to it. A greatwood rod carries two and a half times what a stick will, which is the difference between working and stopping to wait.
research.alchemia.warp.page: Look too long into what should not be, and it begins looking back. The damage is not to the world but to the one studying it, and it does not undo itself with rest.
research.alchemia.water_jug.page: A jug of baked clay that is never empty. Dip a bucket or a bottle in it and it comes away full. Left alone it tops up anything round it that holds water -- a crucible, a cauldron -- a quarter of a bucket every quarter of a second, and fills itself again from the aqua in the air.
scan.alchemia.nothing_there: There is nothing there to read.
warp.alchemia.text.0: You feel like you are being watched.
warp.alchemia.text.1: Something moves at the edge of your sight.
warp.alchemia.text.10: Darkness closes without waiting for night.
warp.alchemia.text.11: What ails you is looking for company.
warp.alchemia.text.12: You are no longer entirely alone in here.
warp.alchemia.text.13: Whatever you look at, looks back.
warp.alchemia.text.2: For a moment, nothing is where you left it.
warp.alchemia.text.3: The air itself feels thin and wrong.
warp.alchemia.text.4: Something is seeping out of you.
warp.alchemia.text.5: A hunger takes you that food will not answer.
warp.alchemia.text.6: You hear your own name, spoken wrong.
warp.alchemia.text.7: The silence has a shape to it.
warp.alchemia.text.8: Your eyes will not settle on anything.
warp.alchemia.text.9: The sun looks at you and does not approve.
